answer: Peer-prediction scoring inside a reputation market: each work item, a marble slab, travels a trellis of independent grader agents who never see each other's verdicts. Payouts use a proper scoring rule comparing every grade against the correlated panel consensus, so accurate graders earn a bonus while lazy rubber-stampers earn nothing. The crystal-clear bite: standing up thousands of fake graders costs compute plus a staked deposit per identity, yet fakes hold no independent information, so clustered votes correlate trivially and pay near zero, and random votes forfeit the bonus every round.
